### 1. **How the `init` command is implemented** (lines 74-102)

The `cmdInit` function:

- Checks if the file already exists and refuses to overwrite it

- Writes the template to the target file

### 2. **How the `--ci` flag is processed** (lines 87-100)

- **Parsing**: In `parseArgs()` (lines 52-72), boolean flags (those without a value) are set to `true` in the flags map
- **Detection**: `cmdInit` checks `args.flags.has('ci')` (line 87) to determine if the flag was passed
- **What it does**: When present, it triggers the workflow file creation logic

### 3. **Conditions for workflow file creation** (lines 87-100)

The workflow file is created only if:
1. The `--ci` flag is present
2. `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` does NOT already exist
   - If it exists, the creation is skipped and a message is logged
   - If it doesn't exist, the directory is created recursively

### 4. **Specific logic for `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` creation** (lines 88-99)

```
- Constructs paths:
  - wfDir = `.github/workflows` (relative to cwd)
  - wfPath = `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml`

- Attempts fs.access(wfPath) to check if it exists:
  - If exists: logs error message and skips
  - If doesn't exist: proceeds

- Creates directory with `fs.mkdir(wfDir, { recursive: true })`

- Customizes workflow content:
  - If output file is default 'FRAI-SPEC.md': uses CI_WORKFLOW constant as-is
  - Otherwise: replaces 'FRAI-SPEC.md' in CI_WORKFLOW with the custom output filename

- Writes workflow to file with fs.writeFile(wfPath, workflow)
```

17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 128 129 ### `frai setup` 130 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 131 132 ### `frai config` 133 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 134 135 ### `frai docs` 136 Utilities for generated artefacts: 137 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 138 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 139 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 140 141 ### `frai rag index [options]` 142 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 143 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 144 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 145 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 146 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 147 148 ### `frai eval` 149 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 150 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 151 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 152 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 153 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 154 155 ### `frai finetune` 156 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 157 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 158 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 159 160 ### `frai update` 161 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 162 163 --- 164 165 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 166 167 Install from npm: 168 ```bash 169 pnpm add frai-core 170 ``` 171 172 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 173 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 174 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 175 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 176 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 177 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 178 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 179 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 180 181 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 182 183 ```ts 184 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 185 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 186 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 187 188 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 189 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 190 }); 191 192 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 193 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 194 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 195 196 await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist); 197 await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard); 198 await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile); 199 await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2)); 200 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext); 201 ``` 202 203 Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products. 204 205 --- 206 207 ## Using `frai-agent` 208 209 `frai-agent` is a LangChain-powered conversational agent that wraps FRAI scanning and documentation workflows behind a natural language interface. It provides an intelligent assistant that can scan repositories, generate documentation, and answer questions about your AI features. 210 211 ### Getting Started 212 213 From the monorepo root: 214 ```bash 215 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repository and summarize AI risks." 216 ``` 217 218 ### Interactive Mode 219 220 Launch a chat-style session: 221 ```bash 222 pnpm agent:frai --interactive --verbose 223 ``` 224 225 The agent supports two tools: 226 - **`scan_repository`** – Scans your codebase for AI indicators using FRAI's static detectors. 227 - **`generate_responsible_ai_docs`** – Generates `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md` from questionnaire answers. 228 229 ### Example Usage 230 231 Scan a repository: 232 ```bash 233 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repo and tell me what AI-related code you found." 234 ``` 235 236 Generate documentation (with questionnaire answers): 237 ```bash 238 pnpm agent:frai "Generate the docs with these answers: { 239 \"core\": { \"name\": \"ReviewCopilot\", \"purpose\": \"assistant\" }, 240 \"impact\": { \"stakeholders\": [\"developers\"], \"impactLevel\": \"medium\" }, 241 \"data\": { \"sources\": [\"internal docs\"], \"retention\": \"30 days\" }, 242 \"performance\": { \"metrics\": [\"accuracy\"] }, 243 \"monitoring\": { \"strategy\": \"daily review\" }, 244 \"bias\": { \"mitigations\": [\"red teaming\"] } 245 }" 246 ``` 247 248 ### API Usage 249 250 ```ts 251 import { createFraIAgentExecutor } from "frai-agent"; 252 253 const executor = await createFraIAgentExecutor({ 254 model: "gpt-4o-mini", 255 verbose: true 256 }); 257 258 const result = await executor.invoke({ 259 input: "scan the repository", 260 chat_history: [] 261 }); 262 263 console.log(result.output); 264 ``` 265 266 `frai-agent` reuses FRAI's configuration system, so it automatically discovers your `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env` or global config. 267 268 --- 269 270 ## Responsible AI Gate (`frai gate`) 271 272 **The idea in one sentence: an AI feature spec is not done until seven responsible-AI questions are answered, and the gate blocks the build until they are.** 273 274 275 276 The seven checks: **risk tier** (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk needs a named human sign-off) · **data & privacy** · **human oversight** · **evaluation thresholds** · **bias & fairness** · **monitoring & rollback** · **transparency & incidents**. Verdicts: ✅ PASS · ⚠️ WARN · ⛔ BLOCK (exit 1). 277 278 ### Add it to any app in 60 seconds 279 280 Works in any repo - new app, existing app, any language: 281 282 ```bash 283 npx frai-gate init --ci 284 ``` 285 286 That drops `FRAI-SPEC.md` (a spec template with the gate built in) and a GitHub Action that runs the gate on every PR. Answer the gate, then: 287 288 ```bash 289 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md 290 ``` 291 292 No API key needed for the check. Two smarter commands use a read-only agent (Claude Code auth or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`): 293 294 ```bash 295 npx frai-gate draft # scans YOUR code and drafts the gate answers from it, 296 # with file:line citations and NEEDS HUMAN INPUT markers 297 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # adversarial review: catches vague answers and 298 # spec claims your code contradicts 299 ``` 300 301 ### If you build with AI coding agents 302 303 ```bash 304 npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills 305 ``` 306 307 installs the `responsible-ai-spec` skill: every spec your agent writes includes the gate, and the agent is forbidden from self-approving high-risk features - a named human signs. Claude Code users in this repo also get `/rai-spec`. 308 309 Everything is also available as `frai gate ...` inside the main CLI, and programmatically via `import { validateSpec } from 'frai-gate'`. Worked example (the one from the demo video): [`examples/support-triage-demo/`](examples/support-triage-demo). Design notes: `docs/rai-gate-design.md`. 310 311 --- 312 313 ## Local Development 314 315 Clone the repository and work from source: 316 ```bash 317 pnpm install 318 pnpm --filter frai run build 319 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 320 ``` 321 322 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 323 ```bash 324 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 325 # then 326 frai --setup 327 ``` 328 329 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 330 331 --- 332 333 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 334 335 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 336 337 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 338 2. Build the CLI: 339 ```bash 340 pnpm --filter frai run build 341 ``` 342 3. Publish `frai-core` first, then `frai`: 343 ```bash 344 cd packages/frai-core && npm publish 345 cd ../frai-cli && npm publish 346 ``` 347 4. Verify on npm: 348 ```bash 349 npm view frai versions --json 350 npm view frai-core versions --json 351 ``` 352 353 --- 354 355 ## Learn More 356 - Website: [frai.cc](https://frai.cc) 357 - NPM package: [frai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai) 358 - docs/ai_feature_backlog.md – roadmap for AI capabilities. 359 - docs/eval_harness_design.md – evaluation harness design notes. 360 - docs/architecture-target.md – monorepo architecture. 361 362 *Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence* 363

1	# frai-gate
2	
3	The **FRAI Gate** (Responsible AI Gate) for specs - part of [FRAI](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai).
4	
5	Every spec for an AI-touching feature must contain a complete `## FRAI Gate`
6	section - seven checks - and implementation doesn't start until the gate passes:
7	
8	1. Risk tier (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk requires a named human sign-off)
9	2. Data provenance & privacy
10	3. Human oversight
11	4. Evaluation plan (numeric thresholds)
12	5. Bias & fairness
13	6. Monitoring & rollback
14	7. Transparency & incident response
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```bash
19	npx frai-gate init --ci                 # scaffold FRAI-SPEC.md + a GitHub Action that runs
20	                                        # the gate on every PR (works in any repo)
21	npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md         # deterministic validation - no API key needed
22	npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # + adversarial AI review of answer quality
23	npx frai-gate draft                     # read-only agent scans the repo and drafts a
24	                                        # gate section grounded in your actual code
25	```
26	
27	Also available as `frai gate ...` from the main [frai CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai).
28	
29	Exit codes: `0` PASS/WARN · `1` BLOCK · `2` usage/error - drop `frai-gate check` straight into CI.
30	
31	`draft` and `--smart` run on the [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk)
32	with read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) and need Claude Code authentication or
33	`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Override the model with `FRAI_GATE_MODEL` (default `claude-opus-5`).
34	
35	> **Privacy note:** `draft` and `--smart` send the repository content the agent reads to
36	> Anthropic's API. The agent is instructed never to read secret material (`.env`, keys,
37	> certificates, credential stores), but treat that as a mitigation, not a guarantee -
38	> think before running them on highly sensitive repos. `check` without `--smart` makes
39	> no network calls at all.
40	
41	## Programmatic API
42	
43	```ts
44	import { validateSpec, draftGateSection, smartReview } from 'frai-gate';
45	
46	const result = validateSpec(await fs.readFile('FRAI-SPEC.md', 'utf8'));
47	// { verdict: 'PASS' | 'WARN' | 'BLOCK', tier, findings, gateSection }
48	```
49	
50	The companion agent skill lives in
51	[sebuzdugan/frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills)
52	(`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`).

# Fix Plan: frai gate init --ci not creating workflow file

## Context
When running `frai gate init --ci` from frai-cli, the GitHub Actions workflow file (`.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml`) is not created, though the spec template is. Running `frai-gate init --ci` directly works correctly. The issue is that frai-cli doesn't pass the `--ci` flag through to the frai-gate subprocess.

## Root Cause
In `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 737-755), the `gate` command is defined with a variadic positional argument pattern `[args...]`. Commander.js treats this specially—it only captures positional arguments, not option flags. When a user runs `frai gate init --ci`:

1. Commander parses this as: command='gate', positional args=['init']
2. The `--ci` flag is recognized as an option but NOT captured in the args array due to the variadic pattern
3. Only `['init']` is passed to spawnSync, losing the flag
4. frai-gate subprocess receives no --ci flag, so it skips workflow creation

The frai-gate parser itself (`packages/frai-gate/src/cli.ts:52-72`) correctly handles flags—the problem is purely in how frai-cli captures and passes them.

## Solution
Explicitly define all flag options that the gate subcommand supports, then reconstruct the full argv array (including flags) to pass to the subprocess.

### Flags to support (from frai-gate help):
- `init`: `--out <file>`, `--ci`
- `check`: `--smart`, `--json`
- `draft`: `--out <file>`, `--print`

## Implementation
Modify the `gate` command in `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` to:

1. Keep the positional `[args...]` but add explicit option definitions:
   - `.option('--ci', 'Create GitHub Actions workflow')`
   - `.option('--smart', 'Add AI quality review')`
   - `.option('--json', 'Machine-readable output')`
   - `.option('--out <file>', 'Output file')`
   - `.option('--print', 'Print to stdout')`

2. In the action handler, reconstruct the full argv from both positional args and the options object, then pass to spawnSync

3. Example reconstruction:
   ```typescript
   const argv = ['init'];
   if (options.ci) argv.push('--ci');
   if (options.out) argv.push('--out', options.out);
   // etc.
   ```

## Critical Files
- **Primary**: `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 737-755 — the gate command definition and action handler)
- **Reference**: `packages/frai-gate/src/cli.ts` (lines 29-44 — help text showing all supported flags; lines 52-72 — the parseArgs function that shows how flags are expected)

## Verification
1. Rebuild frai-cli with `pnpm --filter frai build`
2. Run: `node <repo>/packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js gate init --ci` in a test directory
3. Confirm `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` is created (in addition to `FRAI-SPEC.md`)
4. Test other flag combinations: `--out custom.md`, `check <file> --smart`, `draft --print`

**Solution**: Use `process.argv` directly to capture all arguments after the `gate` command, including both positional arguments and flags, and pass them unchanged to the frai-gate subprocess.
